At parent: B608 'Possible SQL injection vector through string-based query construction.' is reported at line 1 and the process exits 1, even though the suppression comment is on the closing line of the multi-line string (output even says 'Total lines skipped (#nosec): 1'). At fix: no finding, exit 0.

Only line 1 (the opening line of the multi-line string) is consulted for a suppression comment.
verified: Parent (7e6f580): grep shows bandit/core/tester.py contains 'context_tests = self.nosec_lines.get(context["lineno"], None)' and no get_nosec() exists in bandit/core/utils.py -> baby buggy code present. CLI repro exits 1 with the B608 issue listed; project regression test (fix-version example/test checked out onto parent) FAILED. install_recipe: apt-get install -y git && pip install setuptools pbr wheel && pip install --no-build-isolation -e . && pip install --no-build-isolation -e '.[baseline]' && pip install coverage fixtures stestr testscenarios testtools beautifulsoup4. (Plain 'pip install -e .' fails because pbr needs the git repo + a git binary to compute the dev version; setup.py uses pbr so git must exist in the image. bandit itself requires PyYAML, stevedore, rich; installed automatically.)
issue_paraphrase: When a static-analysis warning covers a multi-line string or expression, placing the suppress comment on the closing line of that construct does not silence the warning; the scanner still reports the finding. Users must happen to put the comment on the very first line of the construct. A suppression comment should be honored no matter which line of the flagged code region it appears on.
fix_summary: Introduced utils.get_nosec() which scans the whole context linerange (not just node.lineno) for a # nosec comment, so a suppress comment anywhere in a multi-line expression is honored; also moved 'nosec without test number' bookkeeping from pre-visit to the test phase so a nosec on a later line of a multi-line string is not double counted.
notes: Functional tests must run from the repo root (they use os.getcwd() to locate examples/ and plugins). The single golden test takes ~0.02s at 1 CPU; the full tests/functional/test_functional.py suite runs bandit per example and takes a few minutes at 1 CPU, no network needed. If the harness container runs as root, set PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/pycache so the checkout is not polluted with root-owned __pycache__ directories.

reproduction:
File values.py:
    import sqlite3
    conn = sqlite3.connect("app.db")
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO foo VALUES(%s)" % value)

Run: bandit -q values.py
At parent: no issues reported, exit 0 (a SQL-injection-vector statement with VALUES( and no space is silently missed). At fix: '>> Issue: [B608:hardcoded_sql_expressions] Possible SQL injection vector through string-based query construction.' Location values.py:4, exit 1.

Golden test (from repo root): python -m unittest tests.functional.test_functional.FunctionalTests.test_sql_statements (needs fix-version examples/sql_statements.py and tests/functional/test_functional.py), FAILS at parent, OK at fix.
observed_failure_at_parent: bandit -q values.py exits 0 and reports no issues for 'INSERT INTO foo VALUES(%s)' % value; the sanitized-output listing shows no finding for the VALUES( (no-space) form while the spaced form VALUES ( is still flagged. unittest ...test_sql_statements FAILED (expected counts mismatch) when run with the fix-version example and test.
verified: Parent (b790ce2): bandit/plugins/injection_sql.py line 77 has the SQL regex branch 'insert\s+into\s.*values\s' (requires whitespace after VALUES); CLI repro exits 0 with no finding; fix-version example+test checked out onto parent -> test_sql_statements FAILED. Fix (3c56109): regex branch is 'insert\s+into\s.*values[\s(]'; same CLI repro reports B608 and exits 1; same unittest OK.
install_recipe: apt-get install -y git && pip install setuptools pbr wheel && pip install --no-build-isolation -e . && pip install --no-build-isolation -e '.[baseline]' && pip install coverage fixtures stestr testscenarios testtools beautifulsoup4. (Plain 'pip install -e .' fails because pbr needs the git repo + a git binary to compute the dev version; setup.py uses pbr so git must exist in the image.)
issue_paraphrase: A static-analysis warning for string-built SQL is not raised when an INSERT statement writes VALUES directly before the opening parenthesis with no space (a common style), so a statement that embeds unsanitized input inside a SQL string can pass a scan without any warning even though the same statement with VALUES followed by a space is flagged. Both spellings are valid SQL and should be detected equally.
fix_summary: Changed the SIMPLE_SQL_RE branch for INSERT statements from 'insert\s+into\s.*values\s' to 'insert\s+into\s.*values[\s(]' so that 'VALUES(' with no whitespace also matches, and added positive/negative functional examples.
notes: Functional tests must run from the repo root. The single golden test takes ~0.01s at 1 CPU. No network needed. Selecting the right check is easy by diffing parent vs fix behavior on the repro; the safest correct fix is to widen the regex to accept '(' right after VALUES.

    from django.contrib.auth.models import User
    User.objects.annotate(val=RawSQL(sql="{}secure".format("no"), params=[]))

Run: bandit django_raw.py
At parent: '\n[tester]\tERROR\tBandit internal error running: django_rawsql_used on file django_raw.py at line 3: list index out of range' with IndexError traceback, and no B611 finding (exit 0 with -q). Golden test (from repo root): python -m unittest tests.functional.test_functional.FunctionalTests.test_django_sql_injection_raw (needs fix-version examples/django_sql_injection_raw.py and tests/functional/test_functional.py), FAILS at parent, OK at fix.
observed_failure_at_parent: bandit django_raw.py prints '[tester]\tERROR\tBandit internal error running: django_rawsql_used on file django_raw.py at line 3: list index out of range' plus traceback 'IndexError: list index out of range', and reports no issue for the RawSQL call. unittest ...test_django_sql_injection_raw FAILED (MEDIUM 4 expected vs 6) with fix-version example/test checked out.
verified: Parent (6d6ec6d): bandit/plugins/django_sql_injection.py line 132 reads 'sql = context.node.args[0]' unconditionally; CLI repro produces the internal-error IndexError and no finding; fix-version example+test checked out onto parent -> unittest FAILED. Fix (c420d1d): plugin falls back to keywords2dict(context.node.keywords) when args is empty; CLI repro reports B611 and exits 1; same unittest OK.
install_recipe: apt-get install -y git && pip install setuptools pbr wheel && pip install --no-build-isolation -e . && pip install --no-build-isolation -e '.[baseline]' && pip install coverage fixtures stestr testscenarios testtools beautifulsoup4. (Plain 'pip install -e .' fails because pbr needs the git repo + a git binary to compute the dev version; setup.py uses pbr so git must exist in the image.)
issue_paraphrase: Calling Django's raw-SQL helper with the SQL text passed as a keyword argument instead of as the first positional argument makes the analyzer fail internally: it logs a list-index error with a traceback while scanning the file, and the risky call is not reported at all. A vulnerable raw-SQL call should be flagged regardless of whether its arguments are passed positionally or by keyword.
fix_summary: In the django_rawsql_used plugin, fall back to reading the 'sql' keyword argument (via keywords2dict) when the call has no positional args, so RawSQL(sql=..., params=[...]) is detected instead of raising IndexError.
notes: Functional tests must run from the repo root. Single golden test ~0.01s at 1 CPU. No network (scanning is static; django need not be installed). Note the plugin only fires when 'django.db.models' is imported in the scanned file, so a repro must include the import.

File empty_list.py:
    import subprocess
    subprocess.check_output([], stdout=None)

Run: bandit empty_list.py
At parent: '[tester]\tERROR\tBandit internal error running: start_process_with_partial_path on file ./empty_list.py at line 2: list index out of range' plus traceback 'IndexError: list index out of range'. At fix: the same scan produces no internal error (only the ordinary B404/B603 findings).

Reproduction check: bandit empty_list.py 2>&1 | grep -c 'internal error'  -> 1 at parent, 0 at fix. NOTE: the project's own functional test (test_subprocess_shell) does NOT discriminate this fix, because the crash is caught and logged and the issue counts are identical with and without it; the oracle must be the absence of the 'Bandit internal error' log line.
observed_failure_at_parent: [tester]\tERROR\tBandit internal error running: start_process_with_partial_path on file ./empty_list.py at line 2: list index out of range, followed by File 'bandit/plugins/injection_shell.py', line 687, in start_process_with_partial_path -> node = node.elts[0] -> IndexError: list index out of range. Test count check: test_subprocess_shell passes both at parent and fix code (verified empirically), so the golden check must be the stderr log.
verified: Parent (ad56c78): bandit/plugins/injection_shell.py line 686 reads 'if isinstance(node, ast.List):' with no emptiness guard, node.elts[0] raises IndexError on an empty list; CLI repro logs the internal error with traceback. Fix (049eba0): line reads 'if isinstance(node, ast.List) and node.elts:'; same CLI repro logs no internal error (grep -c 'internal error' = 0). Both directions observed in container on bench-base:python-3.12.
install_recipe: apt-get install -y git && pip install setuptools pbr wheel && pip install --no-build-isolation -e . && pip install --no-build-isolation -e '.[baseline]' && pip install coverage fixtures stestr testscenarios testtools beautifulsoup4. (Plain 'pip install -e .' fails because pbr needs the git repo + a git binary to compute the dev version; setup.py uses pbr so git must exist in the image.)
issue_paraphrase: Scanning a file that calls a subprocess helper with an empty argument list causes the analyzer to log an internal error with a list-index-out-of-range traceback during the scan. It keeps going, but a noisy, unexplained internal error is a sign the analyzer cannot handle valid Python that passes an empty list to these helpers; such calls should scan without any internal error.
fix_summary: Added 'and node.elts' to the isinstance(ast.List) guard in start_process_with_partial_path in the injection_shell plugin so an empty list argument is not indexed, avoiding the IndexError; also added the example line subprocess.check_output([], stdout=None).
notes: The project's regression test for this commit only bumps expected counts in test_subprocess_shell and does not catch the removed crash; an authoring oracle should grep the bandit stderr for 'Bandit internal error' / 'list index out of range' rather than rely on unittest counts. Scan of a 2-line file takes <1s at 1 CPU. No network needed.
